about: Final court convictions of Presidents and Vice Presidents, maintained by hand and reviewed before publishing. Only convictions are listed: charges, pending cases, acquittals, dismissals and allegations are not. Each entry names the court and date and links a public source; corrections go through the app's Report an error page.

entries.sentence: Reclusion perpetua and forfeiture of assets found to be ill-gotten
entries.sentence_tl: Reclusion perpetua at pagkumpiska ng mga ari-ariang napatunayang nakaw
entries.when: For acts during his presidency (1998–2001); decided after he left office
entries.when_tl: Para sa mga ginawa noong siya ay Pangulo (1998–2001); napagpasyahan matapos siyang umalis sa puwesto
entries.later: Granted executive clemency (pardon) by President Gloria Macapagal Arroyo on October 25, 2007
entries.later_tl: Pinatawad (executive clemency) ni Pangulong Gloria Macapagal Arroyo noong Oktubre 25, 2007
entries.source: Wikipedia – Joseph Estrada (public, cites the court decision and news reports)

entries.offense: Failure to file income tax returns (1982–1985), National Internal Revenue Code
entries.offense_tl: Hindi paghahain ng income tax return (1982–1985), National Internal Revenue Code
entries.court: Quezon City Regional Trial Court; affirmed by the Court of Appeals (1997)
entries.sentence: The Court of Appeals kept the conviction for failure to file but removed the prison term and ordered fines; he was cleared of failure to pay the taxes
entries.sentence_tl: Pinanatili ng Court of Appeals ang hatol sa hindi paghahain pero inalis ang pagkakakulong at pinagmulta siya; napawalang-sala siya sa hindi pagbabayad ng buwis
entries.when: As Vice Governor and Governor of Ilocos Norte, before his presidency
entries.when_tl: Noong Bise Gobernador at Gobernador ng Ilocos Norte, bago naging Pangulo
entries.later: COMELEC ruled in 2022 that this did not bar him from running for President
entries.later_tl: Ipinasya ng COMELEC noong 2022 na hindi ito hadlang sa kanyang pagtakbo bilang Pangulo
entries.source: Wikipedia – Bongbong Marcos (public, cites the court decisions and COMELEC rulings)
